THIS SITE IS THE ATLAS'S HONEST FAILURE, AND IT IS IN THE ATLAS FOR THAT REASON.

Utzon's shells are spherical sections cut from one sphere of a cited 75.2 m radius, standing on edge and leaning. A `Dome` is an ellipsoidal cap standing on its own base; it cannot lean, and it cannot be a section of a sphere it does not contain. What is built here is three domes of the right size in the right places on a podium of the cited footprint, rising to the cited 67 m -- and it is not the Sydney Opera House. It is the shape this vocabulary produces when asked for one.

The alternative was to leave the site out. Leaving it out would say the Atlas can build anything it contains; putting it in says what the Atlas cannot do, which is the more useful claim and costs a shot rather than a lie. `1,056,006 tiles in two colours` -- the building is itself a mosaic of over a million modules, which makes the failure sharper rather than softer.
